content.comment_body: Could someone assist me in identifying the version of this [product_name] device? On the actual hardware, the label shows [article_no]. However, the website displays different information. This thread was split from another related to a persistent login issue.
I'm unclear on what you're asking from me. Consider opening a support request. Maybe [company_name] can provide better assistance regarding your issue.

Don't worry, I usually manage troubleshooting on my own. I have two different [product_name] devices: one has a type number ending in [article_no] (possibly [version_no]), the other ends with [article_no] (enabled for cloud features, likely [version_no]). The web server for both shows: Device Series [product_name] [article_no] Device Type [version_no] Firmware [version_no], and another Device Series [product_name] [article_no] Device Type [version_no] Firmware [version_no] — both reveal the same series number via the internal web page, which makes the numbering logic confusing, especially when the etched hardware series number doesn’t line up with the online version.

analysis.insight_summary: Users find the versioning schemes for [product_name] unclear, as physical labels and web interface data often do not match. This creates confusion around device identification and feature compatibility. Additionally, users are frustrated by inconsistent web session behavior, which relies on browser cookie management. Concerns exist about [company_name]'s product support, quality assurance, and clear communication about hardware versioning as well as session management features.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want transparent mapping between device model numbers, firmware versions, and details shown in internal interfaces. They also expect consistent session persistence and clarity when using the 'keep me logged on' feature via the web interface.
